jobs.description:
Company Description

Classic Fire + Life Safety is an industry leader in fire protection and life safety services, supporting commercial, industrial, and institutional clients across Canada. With a strong reputation built on safety, reliability, and technical expertise, the company continues to scale through organic growth, value accretive acquisitions and partnerships, and operational excellence.

Our goal is to partner with our customers, to ensure their building, and the people in them are safe, from new building construction activities, modernization activities, and demand for system upgrades, through to preventative maintenance and service

Why join the Classic team?

CFLS is a caring company who values our staff.
CFLS is local and is part of the community.
CFLS is a full-service fire protection contractor.

Overview

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Vice President, Financial Controller to lead the controllership, accounting, treasury, tax, audit, compliance, and shared services functions while acting as a key strategic partner to the CFO and executive leadership team.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Financial Controller is responsible for the integrity of the company's financial reporting, internal controls, treasury management, tax compliance, and accounting operations.

The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting expertise with practical functional leadership. This individual will oversee all financial control activities while driving process improvements, automation, systems optimization, and finance transformation initiatives that support continued growth.

This role requires a leader who can operate both strategically and tactically, providing executive-level guidance while remaining close to the details.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Controllership

Own all monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes.
Ensure timely and accurate consolidation of financial results across all business units.
Support preparation of management reporting packages, lender, and board reporting.
Ensure compliance with Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE), IFRS (if applicable), GAAP, and regulatory requirements.
Develop and maintain accounting policies and technical accounting guidance.

Internal Controls, Governance & Risk Management

Design, implement, and continuously enhance internal control frameworks.
Lead annual audit planning and execution.
Coordinate relationships with external auditors and advisors.
Oversee risk management initiatives related to financial governance and credit agreement compliance.

Shared Services & Transactional Finance

Provide leadership over:
Accounts Receivable / Collections
Accounts Payable
Master Data Governance

Establish service-level expectations and performance metrics.
Improve efficiency through process standardization and automation.
Improve data quality and financial discipline throughout the organization

Treasury & Cash Management

Oversee corporate treasury operations and liquidity management.
Monitor working capital performance and cash flow forecasting.
Manage banking relationships and lender compliance requirements.
Optimize cash management structures across multiple legal entities.
Support debt financing initiatives and covenant reporting.

Tax Leadership

Oversee corporate income tax, sales tax, and other statutory compliance requirements.
Manage year-end tax provisions and related disclosures.
Ensure compliance across all provinces and jurisdictions in which the company operates.

Acquisition Integration

Support accounting integration of acquired businesses.
Standardize financial reporting and control environments following acquisitions.
Ensure successful transfer of accounting and reporting processes into the corporate finance structure.

Leadership & Talent Development

Lead, mentor, and develop the finance organization.
Establish performance standards and succession plans.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Recruit and develop future finance leaders.

Qualifications

Required

CPA designation (CPA, CA preferred).
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Minimum 12-15 years of progressive finance and accounting experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior leadership role such as: Controller, Director of Finance, VP Finance, VP Controller.
Experience in cross-border, multi-site service environments, such as field services, facilities services, industrial services, or related sectors.
Financial reporting knowledge.
Strong understanding of: Revenue recognition, Work-in-progress accounting, Project accounting, Audit and internal controls, Treasury management, Corporate taxation
Experience with ERP implementations and finance transformation initiatives.
Advanced Excel and financial systems capabilities.

Leadership Competencies

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

High integrity and sound judgment.
Strong business partnership skills.
Ability to influence across all levels of the organization.
Exceptional communication and presence.
Continuous improvement mindset.

Osborne Financial Search is partnering with a growing Canadian financial services company to find their next Director of Finance.
Our client is a mid-sized, entrepreneurial business that is part of a larger North American group. It has grown quickly in recent years and still has very little bureaucracy. People are encouraged to get involved, and good ideas move fast.

Reporting to the VP Finance, you'll own the company's end-to-end accounting and financial reporting and act as the VP's right hand. You'll lead an experienced accounting team, working closely with the parent company's corporate finance group.

CPA with 7 to 12 years of progressive experience

A track record of improving processes, shortening the close and strengthening controls

A people leader who earns trust and brings a team along through change

The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we are committed to continually improving our healthcare system. The Department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity

As the Director of Accountability and Analytics
, you will have an opportunity to influence how physician services are planned, funded, monitored and improved across Nova Scotia’s health system.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will be a key member of the leadership team advancing strategic priorities across the physician services portfolio. Your leadership will span two connected areas: strengthening accountability for physician remuneration and funded programs, including support for major negotiations, and building the branch’s data and analytics capability to enable stronger, evidence-informed decisions.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader who is comfortable working at the intersection of policy, funding, accountability, analytics and health-system transformation

Your work will help strengthen performance and accountability while building the data and analytical capabilities needed to support the future of physician services in Nova Scotia.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you will provide strategic leadership to complex initiatives that strengthen accountability and expand the use of data in physician services planning, funding and performance management.

You will lead multidisciplinary teams, establish priorities and create the conditions for high-quality, decision-focused work. Working across the Department, government, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health and external organizations, you will bring partners together to move initiatives from design through implementation, measurement and continuous improvement.

Strengthening accountability by designing and improving frameworks, performance measures and monitoring approaches for physician remuneration models and funded initiatives.

Building trusted partnerships and collaborative approaches to complex issues where perspectives and priorities may differ.
Influencing decisions by translating complex information into clear briefings, presentations and recommendations for senior audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a strategic and collaborative leader who can bring clarity to complex issues and turn evidence into action. is a senior technology leader accountable for the health, reliability, performance and ongoing evolution of Beem’s enterprise-wide Application Services portfolio, which includes core banking, lending, digital banking, enterprise applications, and other assigned business applications. The role ensures these applications remain secure, resilient, current and well supported, providing a dependable and scalable foundation for Beem’s members, employees and business operations. The Director sets the multi-year strategic direction for Application Services and owns the operating model, investment priorities and portfolio decisions within their accountability, shaping how applications are managed and evolved across Beem.

The Director leads multiple teams responsible for application support, configuration, upgrades, patching and testing, operational vendor management, and delivery of small non-material enhancements. The role translates Business and Technology priorities into coordinated application service and lifecycle plans, balancing operational excellence with application simplification, automation, responsible AI and continuous improvement to reduce friction, improve efficiency and enable Beem’s digital-first and people-first ambitions.

This is a hybrid position, and preference will be given to applicants located in British Columbia. In-person interview(s) will be required during the later stages of the recruitment process, with location(s) to be determined.

What you’ll do:

Leadership and Team Success

As a member of the Technology Leadership team, accountability for the decisions connecting application services priorities to member outcomes, business needs and Beem’s strategic direction.
Leads Beem’s Application Services portfolio, building high-performing teams and establishing clear accountability and service ownership across the applications, while fostering collaboration, curiosity and continuous improvement.

Strengthens application observability, runbooks, known-error records and knowledge practices to identify issues earlier and improve first-contact resolution.
Partners with business continuity, disaster recovery and Technology teams to validate application recovery readiness, test critical dependencies and address resilience gaps.

Application Lifecycle & Change Delivery

Develops and maintains an enterprise-wide rolling multi-year application service and lifecycle roadmap aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture and technology plans, balancing currency, resilience, supportability and cost.
Provides recommendations on application consolidation, retirement and standardization to reduce duplication, technical debt and operational complexity, with investment and architecture decisions made through established governance.
Leads vendor upgrades and patches through impact assessment, regression testing, cutover and stabilization, maintaining visibility into version currency, end-of-support exposure and remediation plans.
Delivers configuration changes and small enhancements on non-material initiatives, coordinating dependencies, release readiness and stakeholder communication to minimize member and employee disruption.

Introduces approved AI-enabled and automated practices for activities such as ticket triage, knowledge management, release analysis and regression testing, with human accountability and appropriate oversight.
Partners with business owners, Enterprise Transformation & Integration, and Technology teams to translate process improvements into supportable application changes, while preserving clear business, delivery and operational accountabilities.
Measures whether improvements reduce manual effort, recurring demand and service delays, and redirects released capacity toward higher-value work and priority commitments.

Partners with business and product teams to understand how application services enable everyday banking, digital engagement and advice-led relationships, translating those needs into clear operational priorities.
Collaborates with Architecture, Information Security, Infrastructure and Operations, Engineering, and Data teams to manage application dependencies and support consistent, reliable experiences across channels.
Owns and manages operational vendor relationships, holding providers accountable for service commitments, issue resolution, release coordination and transparent escalation.
Responsible for application cost, usage and service insights to support budget planning, procurement decisions and vendor assessments.
Maintains visibility into application risks, control gaps and remediation commitments, providing decision-ready reporting on service health, lifecycle exposure, vendor performance, capacity and improvement outcomes.
Owns remediation commitments for application risks and controls gaps for their portfolio.

10+ years of progressive experience in application support, application management or IT service delivery, including senior people leadership experience.
Deep experience supporting business-critical applications in financial services, ideally including core banking, lending and digital banking platforms.
Strong grounding in service management practices, including incident, problem, change and release management; ITIL certification or equivalent experience is an asset.
Proven experience managing application vendors, service-level performance, escalations and upgrade coordination.
Demonstrated success planning and delivering application upgrades with disciplined regression testing and minimal member impact.
Experience with AI-enabled or agentic applications in production, or a strong interest in building this capability, including monitoring, evaluation and responsible change control.
Understanding of operational resilience, risk and control expectations within a regulated financial institution.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across business and technical partners.
Working knowledge of modern service management and monitoring tools, such as ITSM platforms, application monitoring and observability tools, Azure DevOps or Jira.

Total Rewards:

Health & Wellness: Extended health coverage (including mental health support), dental care, and disability coverage

Beem Member Perks: Free banking accounts, special mortgage and lending rates, and preferred financial perks

Build Together: You are a team player who thrives on collaboration, sparks ideas, and fosters inclusivity.
Own It: You are ready to take charge, drive change, and deliver outstanding results.

This role oversees IT operations, business applications, vendor partnerships, cybersecurity and in-flight technology initiatives within a Microsoft-centred environment that includes Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform. Technology Leadership & Execution

Serves as the senior technology advisor to the Chief Financial Officer and leadership team, providing clear, concise updates and recommendations.

Ensures technology priorities remain aligned with organizational goals and carries forward in-flight initiatives to agreed milestones.

Maintains a strong understanding of the organization’s technology environment and remains actively involved in the execution and resolution of day-to-day technology matters.

Identifies opportunities to improve technology effectiveness, reliability and user experience, with a focus on practical solutions appropriate for a 50-100-person organization.

AI Implementation & Adoption

Supports the implementation of agentic AI solutions across the organization, working with business teams and external partners to identify practical use cases, configure and test solutions, and integrate them into everyday workflows.

Manages and supports the Board’s AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, overseeing licensing, access, configuration and technical support.

Coordinates the technical requirements for AI implementation, including system integrations, data access, testing and deployment, ensuring appropriate security controls and human oversight in accordance with the Board’s AI use policy.

Provides practical guidance, training and troubleshooting to help employees adopt AI tools and apply them effectively in their work.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Leads, supports and develops the IT team, setting priorities and managing performance and KPIs.

Provides service to all areas of the Board by applying business partner skills and a client service outlook.

Allocates work effectively across the team and ensures appropriate coverage for operational priorities, projects and employee support.

Documents key decisions and changes to support a smooth transition at the end of the contract

Leads vendor escalations and ensures unresolved service issues are addressed quickly and effectively.

Maintains the Board's cybersecurity posture across Azure and Microsoft 365, including identity, access and data protection.

Upholds IT policies, including the Board's AI use policy, and supports compliance with accessibility (AODA) and privacy requirements.

Proven experience managing managed service providers and external agencies, including contracts and performance.

Solid grounding in cybersecurity practices for a cloud-first organization.

Experience managing an IT budget and reporting to senior executives.

Strong oral and written communication skills; experience explaining technical matters to partners at all levels.

Ability to work cross-functionally and collaboratively with business units.

A steady, pragmatic leader who builds trust quickly with a new team

A business partner first, able to translate organizational needs into practical technology solutions

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Wealth Management is seeking a Head of Data and AI to set the scientific direction and lead the applied AI research and development agenda for our Canadian business. As the senior AI scientist and technical authority on our Wealth Management Data and AI team, you will decide how we solve ML and AI problems rigorously, and how we prove the results are accurate, safe and valuable to advisors and clients.

We are looking for a deeply technical AI leader with a research-grade understanding of modern machine learning and generative AI, and a track record of turning that science into production systems at scale. You will lead and grow a team of AI scientists, ML researchers, data scientists and ML engineers, partner closely with product, technology and business leaders across Wealth Management and RBC, and work with RBC’s broader AI research community to bring frontier techniques into the hands of advisors.

What will you do?

Define and own the AI/ML science roadmap for Wealth Management Canada, covering generative AI, agentic systems, predictive modelling, personalization, forecasting and optimization.
Identify where emerging research (foundation models, reasoning, retrieval, agents, multimodal, small and fine-tuned models) can create a durable advantage in wealth management, and turn it into funded, testable bets.
Make build, buy and fine-tune decisions on models, architectures and platforms based on evidence, benchmarking and a clear view of cost, latency, risk and performance.
Represent Wealth Management’s AI science externally and across RBC, including partnerships with research institutes, universities and technology partners.
Provide hands-on technical leadership across the model lifecycle: problem framing, data and feature design, training, fine-tuning, prompting and orchestration, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
Establish the standards for experimental design, offline and online evaluation, A/B testing and statistical validity, so that results are reproducible and claims are defensible.
Build robust evaluation frameworks for LLM and agent-based systems, including accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, bias, robustness and red-teaming, tied to real advisor workflows.
Review the technical work of scientists and engineers, coach them on research quality, and raise the bar on how models are designed, tested and explained.
Own the scientific approach to responsible AI in a regulated environment, including explainability, fairness, privacy, safety guardrails, model risk and ongoing performance monitoring.
Work with Model Risk, Legal, Compliance, Privacy and Technology to translate emerging regulation and internal policy into practical technical controls and validation methods.
Communicate model capabilities, limitations and uncertainty clearly and honestly to senior leaders, regulators and non-technical stakeholders.
Develop and retain AI scientists, researchers and ML engineers, and create a culture of curiosity, scientific debate and learning by experimentation.
Create career paths and mentoring for technical talent, and build a strong research-to-production pipeline with engineering and product partners.
Champion a test-and-learn approach where hypotheses, experiments and data drive decisions, and where failed experiments are shared and learned from.
Define the data requirements AI needs to succeed, and partner with data and technology teams on high-quality domains, a consistent data dictionary and a unified client view that serve both AI and operational use cases.
Work with product and business leaders across Global Wealth Management, WMC and RBC to translate advisor and client problems into well-posed scientific questions, and scientific results into shipped products.

Advanced degree (Master’s required, PhD strongly preferred) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a related quantitative field;

Experience with responsible AI, explainability, model risk management and AI governance, ideally in a regulated industry;
Strong leadership skills, with experience hiring, coaching and leading high-calibre scientific and engineering talent;
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex scientific concepts and trade-offs to executives and non-technical stakeholders;

Nice-to-have:

Understanding of the banking industry, preferably Wealth Management, is an asset.

new_jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As the Managing Director, XVA Management, you'll provide senior front-office leadership for the pricing, transfer, hedging, and portfolio management of valuation adjustments arising from counterparty credit risk, funding, collateral, initial margin, liquidity, and regulatory capital across Global Markets. You'll lead the Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA), Funding Valuation Adjustment (FVA), and Collateral Valuation Adjustment (ColVA) mandates while supporting the continued evolution of the broader XVA framework, including Margin Valuation Adjustment (MVA) and capital-related valuation adjustments, where applicable. In this role, you'll combine strong trading judgment with strategic leadership to help optimize transaction structuring, improve resource efficiency, and support disciplined risk-taking. You'll oversee desk strategy, financial performance, governance, and infrastructure priorities while building the talent, operating model, and capabilities required to support broader desk-head responsibilities over time.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. To successfully perform the work, you’ll be on-site full-time.

How You'll Succeed

Lead XVA trading and portfolio management - Lead the pricing, risk transfer, hedging, and portfolio management of CVA, FVA, and related valuation adjustments across Global Markets, with accountability for desk profit and loss (P&L), risk appetite, and limit usage.
Deliver strategic transaction advice - Provide timely XVA pricing and strategic transaction guidance to Sales and Trading, including assessment of counterparty credit, funding, collateral, margin, liquidity, and capital impacts.
Manage risk with discipline - Manage material market, credit spread, jump-to-default, wrong-way, basis, funding, and model risks, and establish effective hedging strategies, particularly during periods of market stress.
Oversee desk performance and controls - Oversee daily P&L and risk, explain key drivers and sensitivities, challenge unusual movements, and ensure timely escalation of valuation, model, data, control, or limit issues.
Drive funding and capital efficiency - Partner with Central Funding, Treasury, and Global Markets Resource Optimization to improve funding, collateral, initial margin, leverage, and regulatory capital efficiency across Global Markets.
Strengthen collateral strategy and operating effectiveness - Provide senior oversight and advisory support to the Collateral Operations Group, including guidance on collateral strategy, complex transactions, disputes, control issues, and enhancements to operating effectiveness.
Advance desk strategy and business performance - Own and advance the desk strategy, annual plan, financial objectives, and management reporting, identifying opportunities to improve risk-adjusted returns, client competitiveness, and portfolio diversification.
Translate market and regulatory developments into action - Monitor market practice, competitor activity, and regulatory developments affecting counterparty risk, derivatives valuation, capital, margin, and funding, and turn these developments into clear business actions.
Maintain strong governance - Maintain effective governance for valuation, reserves, risk transfer, new products, and transaction approvals, and represent the desk at relevant risk, valuation, capital, and business governance forums.
Set the direction for analytics and infrastructure - Set priorities for XVA analytics, models, data, and technology, and sponsor automation, scalable controls, and infrastructure enhancements in partnership with Quantitative Analytics, Technology, and Operations.
Act as a trusted senior advisor - Serve as a senior escalation point for complex or material transactions, communicating recommendations, portfolio risks, and performance clearly to Capital Markets senior management and control functions.
Promote a strong risk and team culture - Promote a strong risk and conduct culture, ensure compliance with all applicable governance, control, regulatory, and policy requirements, and build a high-performing, inclusive team through disciplined hiring, coaching, succession planning, performance management, and development.

Who You Are

You have a degree in finance, mathematics, economics, engineering, or a related discipline. An advanced degree or relevant professional designation is an asset.
You have deep senior markets experience. You bring 12 or more years of relevant markets experience, including significant senior XVA trading responsibility and leadership of people, risk, P&L, or a material portfolio.
You bring deep XVA and derivatives expertise. You have strong knowledge of CVA, FVA, ColVA, MVA, and capital-related valuation adjustments, along with counterparty exposure, netting, collateral and margin mechanics, funding, liquidity, and the accounting and regulatory frameworks relevant to derivatives.
You have broad cross-asset knowledge. You bring expertise across interest rates, foreign exchange, credit, equities, and commodities, along with a strong understanding of market, credit spread, jump-to-default, wrong-way, basis, and model risk.
You turn complexity into clear decisions. You can translate complex risk, valuation, and capital considerations into commercial decisions, transaction structures, and clear recommendations for clients and senior management.
You demonstrate sound judgment under pressure. You have a disciplined approach to risk management, a strong control orientation, and the ability to lead through volatile markets and significant incidents.
You have strong strategic planning, financial management, and stakeholder influence skills. You have the credibility to represent the desk in senior governance forums and with control partners.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
You're digitally savvy. You seek out innovative solutions and embrace evolving technologies. You can easily adapt to new tools and trends.
You are an effective communicator. You bring strong negotiation, relationship management, and client service skills, along with a commitment to collaboration, inclusion, and professional conduct.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
